events.title: Business operation declared
events.detail: Trusted application code supplies operation_ref “refund-demo-002” for a ₹100 refund.

events.title: Refund created
events.detail: worker-A reached the provider, which created rfnd_FAKE001 for ₹100. The money moved.

events.title: Worker crashed
events.detail: worker-A died before it could record the outcome. The operation is left in EXECUTING with its lease still held.

events.title: Lease expired
events.detail: No live worker holds the operation any more, so it becomes eligible for recovery.

events.title: New worker started
events.detail: worker-B sweeps for operations whose lease lapsed. It reconstructs the provider call entirely from persisted state -- the caller is not asked to re-submit anything.

events.title: Same business operation loaded
events.detail: worker-B resumed operation_ref “refund-demo-002”. A new worker is not a new financial operation.

events.title: Persisted provider identity reused
events.detail: Recovery sent the stored identity sha256:<fp>. It was never regenerated -- regenerating it here is what would create a second refund.

events.title: Provider invoked
events.detail: Invocation #2 sent to the deterministic provider fixture.

events.title: Original result recovered
events.detail: The provider returned the original rfnd_FAKE001 instead of creating a second refund.

events.title: State: SUCCEEDED
events.detail: One business operation survived a process death: 2 provider invocations, 1 financial effect.
